study type: Before-and-after study; retrospective electronic chart review
exposure: Planned duration of double-balloon catheter placement for cervical ripening (6 hours vs 12 hours)
outcome: Time from balloon placement to vaginal delivery
cohort: The study included 189 analyzable patients with a prior history of cesarean delivery who received a double-balloon catheter for cervical ripening during their trial of labor.
finding: Planned removal of a double-balloon catheter at 6 hours compared to 12 hours for cervical ripening in patients with prior cesarean delivery may result in higher chances of successful vaginal delivery and possibly a shorter time to delivery.
mod_finding: Planned removal of the double-balloon catheter at 6 hours compared to 12 hours did not increase the rates of cesarean delivery.
